drivingQuestion: How can one who gathers bones eat sacrificial food that night if he is corpse-impure?
outcomeNote: Mishna emended: others gathered the bones for him

segments.he: הַשּׁוֹמֵעַ עַל מֵתוֹ וְכוּ׳. מְלַקֵּט עֲצָמוֹת? הָא בָּעֵי הַזָּאַת שְׁלִישִׁי וּשְׁבִיעִי! אֵימָא: שֶׁלִּיקְּטוּ לוֹ עֲצָמוֹת.
segments.en: We learned in the mishna: «One who hears about» the death of «his dead» relative more than thirty days after the death and one who gathers bones immerse and eat sacrificial food in the evening. The Gemara expresses surprise: Can this apply to «one who gathers bones? But» by doing so he came in contact with the bones of a corpse, and «he needs sprinkling on» the «third and seventh» days in order to become ritually pure. The Gemara answers: Emend the teaching of the mishna and instead «say:» One «for whom they gathered bones,» meaning that other people gathered the bones of his parents to transfer them to a new grave but he himself did not touch them, has a rabbinical requirement to observe a day of acute mourning, but he is not ritually impure.

moves.cueHe: מלקט עצמות? הא בעי הזאת שלישי ושביעי
moves.summary: The bone-gatherer is corpse-impure and needs sprinkling
Emend: one for whom others gathered the bones

edges.about: one who gathers bones touches them and needs third- and seventh-day sprinkling, so cannot eat sacrificial food that night
